value.body: Builds machine learning models and puts them into real products — preparing data, training and evaluating models, and deploying them so they run reliably at scale. Employers include product companies, GCCs, the AI teams of IT services firms, and startups. A day mixes Python coding, running experiments, reviewing model results and working with data and software engineers.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech (CSE or AI & ML), B.Sc/M.Sc with strong maths, or MCA
items.note: An M.Tech or MS is common in research-heavy roles

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Python, PyTorch or TensorFlow, SQL, Git, cloud platforms

items.label: Indian tech-sector workforce
items.note: Whole IT-BPM sector, not this role alone

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Few employers hire freshers directly as ML engineers; a common route is to join as a software or data engineer and move into ML work. Strong Python, maths (linear algebra, probability, statistics) and end-to-end projects that deploy a model strengthen applications. Campus placement at product companies and GCCs is another entry point.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry-level openings are fewer than for general software roles, and expectations are high.
Growth path: ML engineer → senior → ML lead or applied scientist.
The field moves fast; many roles now involve adapting large pre-trained models rather than training from scratch.
